keyFindings.description: The categorical extraction prohibition this change ships contradicts four status: active learnings of this repository, one of them on the very binary the change adds, and the sweep that round 1 started stopped after one file. The rule: 'What rules the attempt out is not the filesystem but the next section's ruling: an extraction prefix is the withheld operator-setup capability' (tools.md:45-47), 'An extraction prefix: everything in reach of it' (:90-95), 'Improvising — an extraction prefix, a vendored binary, a hand-rolled substitute — is not the step' (:340), 'never an extraction' (docs/kubernetes.md:184) and 'the withheld operator-setup capability under any reading' (docs/kubernetes.md:191). Against it, each `status: active` and each prescribing exactly that technique: docs/solutions/testing/the-real-dispatch-stack-...-INFRA-42.md:13,30,37 unpacks postgresql-17, postgresql-client-17, libpq5, postgresql-17-pgvector and libicu76 with `dpkg-deb -x` and runs them under LD_LIBRARY_PATH; docs/solutions/testing/a-browser-harness-...-INFRA-43.md:12,36,38, whose line 36 says the extraction 'gives initdb/pg_ctl/psql'; docs/solutions/testing/a-pod-harness-moves-tmpdir-too-...-INFRA-44.md:13,132; docs/solutions/legion/a-port-held-in-an-issue-pod-...-LEGION-695.md:12,39,41. This is round 1's finding 2 with one instance fixed: the author wrote the '**Superseded 2026-10-24 (INFRA-221):**' note on LEGION-748 and did not carry it to these. The consequence is not abstract: the image carries psql but no Postgres server and no pgvector, so the documented way to stand up the Dispatch e2e stack a reader-facing change must pass — the suite this change's own psql justification names — is the recipe tools.md now forbids, with escalation to the architect as the only sanctioned alternative. One of two things must be in the merge: the note the author already wrote applied to those four, or one carve-out sentence in tools.md and in the docs options row naming the harness case and citing them. Which way is the architect's scope call; that it is reconciled is not.

The image-change site list is wrong again, in the paragraph round 5 sent back, and this pull request is again its own counter-example. It says the name goes through 'every site that spells it out' and then 'Three are in packages/daemon/docker/worker.Dockerfile'. Six sites in that file spell the five client names out, and this change edited all of them: :26-27 (the file-header inventory, 489 lines above the apt line and not 'the comment saying why that package is carried'), :417 (the THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES intro string), :455 and :494 (the runtime-stage comments), :644 (the smoke step) and :697 (the probe step's comment). The list names three. A role that works the list adds a sixth client and leaves the Dockerfile's own header saying the image carries five. Outside the Dockerfile the gap is wider still — this change also had to edit docs/kubernetes.md's image-contents list, AGENTS.md:125 and docs/site/src/content/docs/legion/running-legion.md. The fix is to stop enumerating rather than to extend the enumeration: a hand-maintained list of hand-maintained lists drifts the way the lists it describes drift, and it has now been wrong twice — 'five files, because its own tests hold them to each other' in round 5, 'three are in the Dockerfile' in round 6. `grep -rn redis-cli` and carry the new name through everything it finds; only the four Go sites are gated (image.go's toolchain list, capabilities.go's summary, capabilitiestest.go's stubs, image_test.go's expected detail), so missing one of those is red and missing a Dockerfile comment, the notices string or the smoke step opens green and ships a licence file that does not name the package it installs. That is shorter, cannot go stale, and lets AGENTS.md:125 go back to being a pointer. Everything else in the paragraph is right and verified: the four gated sites, and the notices string assembled to /usr/share/doc/legion/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.

Reported, not requested, and it does not meet the bar: 'the cache takes about 20 KB and holds no wheel'. I measured 20 KB; the tester measured 3.5 KB on a fresh cache. The clauses a role acts on — no wheel in the cache, the interpreter under UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR at about 70 MB — reproduced for both of us. Every other number in the file is one reproducible measurement, and a precise-sounding figure two runs disagree on is the one that invites the next round's 'I measured something else'. The architect's own no-number ruling on the ephemeral-storage sentence is the precedent: 'a few kilobytes and holds no wheel', or keep the figure with the uv version it was measured on.

Reported, not requested: the two files now give the same volume two different figures in the same pull request — docs/kubernetes.md:189 'the issue's disk is 49 GiB with 2.5 GiB used', skills/legion-worker/references/tools.md:151 '49 GiB with 5.2 GiB used'. Both were true when measured; neither is wrong in a way a role acts on. Worth one touch while the consolidation is open, since it is the last twinned measurement left after the split.

The branch's newest pull_request run head is the code head f42e46b6a6f4; its check-runs show all four completed/success, with Tests run 40147268875, Legion Envoy and Contracts 40147268977, Docs 40147268925, PR Title 40147269021 and Worker Image 40147268909 all success. compare f42e46b6...5a881239 is `ahead` with only .legion/ files, and GitHub reports the pull request MERGEABLE.
threads: Twenty-nine threads, all of rounds 1 to 5, every one carrying the implementer's disposition and resolved by it. I read round 5's four resolutions against the tree and accept them; I unresolved none. This round's two findings and two reports are new threads.
moveCheck: The consolidation was checked as a move, not read as prose. Of the text removed from docs/kubernetes.md this round, every one of its 77 inline-code spans, all 8 URLs and all 10 numeric figures is present in skills/legion-worker/references/tools.md or in what docs kept; nothing was lost in transit and nothing was slipped into a moved block beyond the three round-5 findings and the architect's no-number ruling. The twelve lines docs gained are the pointer and the verdict clause that anchors the options table that stayed. The pointer direction is single: docs names tools.md once, tools.md names docs for the operator's side, and no 'the fuller account' claim survives in either file. The paragraph tools.md cites for the Playwright install lock is where it says it is — docs/kubernetes.md:2120, inside '### Anatomy of a Sandbox pod' at :1886.
acceptedThisRound: The browser passage: Playwright passes as it stands because playwright-core resolves its registry under XDG_CACHE_HOME, which the runtime puts on the issue's volume, with the shared registry and its install lock named and correctly cited; Puppeteer is the counter-case needing PUPPETEER_CACHE_DIR. packages/dispatch/package.json:15 is the `playwright install` the passage names.
The sharing clause excludes XDG_STATE_HOME by name, with the browser-broker reason the runtime itself gives.
The ephemeral-storage sentence carries no number, as the architect ruled.
The uv paragraph is rewritten to what the two runs actually leave, with the wheel in UV_CACHE_DIR for the library case and the interpreter under UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR for the other.
The consolidation itself: this is the first round that paid the duplication down rather than growing it.
